Rocky Road - Juandré Kidson Murder

By: Floris Kotze | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A father murdered in front of his family, why our roads are dangerous, even when we are not driving.

Unique Selling Point:
In early May, the Kidson couple and their baby were travelling on the Bakwena N4 towards Brits in their Hyundai SUV. Around 20:00 they drove over rocks near the R512/Randburg exit. Knowing it was unsafe, Juandré Kidson kept driving. Until he couldn’t anymore. He had no other option than to stop. He get out of the car to change the wheel. Whilst changing the tyre, 3 men approached their car. Armed and dangerous. Whilst pleading with the men to let his wife and baby go, they shot him in the head in cold blood, in-front of his family. The 3 men tried to take their baby, fighting and struggling with the men, they shot Johanette Kidson, his wife, too. The men then fled empty handed. Both Johanette and her baby survived.
What lead to the brutal murder?
We speak to the Kidson family, at the centre of this tragedy. We will hear in detail what happened on that fateful night.


Summary:
We visit the exact location of where Juandré was murdered next to the N4. His brother Marco, tell us how it changed their lives forever.

We speak to emergency responders about what is called “Spiking”, putting spikes / nails / screws in the road to get you to stop. They tell us what they see on a regular basis.

Bakwena Toll
This area is known for being a hotspot for these incidents with police and the MEC for Community Safety well aware of the dangers. We speak to Bakwena Platinum Corridor Concession Toll, they will give us facts about the accidents that occur, not only on the N4 but surrounding roads too. What are being done to curb this?
Other incidents
We find out that the Kidson incident was the second “Spiking” to occur on that day, on the very same section of road. We hear of other life changing incidents that involved “Spiking” or rocks in the road. A man spent weeks in a coma after perpetrators dropped rocks off a bridge as he passed by.


Further information:
Unique Selling Point
I will approach this as a PSA. It is clear from speaking to people involved, that the tactic of “Spiking” has gotten out of hand in this area. Unlike Kate’s insert, where they damage the car to steal some stuff, this has gotten more brutal, much more dangerous. They murder people for nothing. They wanted to take the baby of the family. They cause accidents and watch the chaos unfold from afar. Some even got arrested and when they got out, the trend continued. They move around, it is not only occurring on the N4, but other roads in the area too.
Private companies have now started to patrol the N4, once again, revealing that the SAPS is not capable of curbing this.
I will use the Kidson family’s as a vehicle to carry the story, but we will reference other incidents that occurred to make the public aware of this.
In the words of Johanette Kidson: “If we only knew that another incident took place on that same road, earlier on the same day, we would have definitely avoided it. Juandré would still be alive.”


Extra Budget Items:
We might shoot at night, perhaps we will need overtime for 1 night for the presenter.

Script:


Opening: Derek Listen to Radio
You hear about the horrors that happen to South Africans…
In this particular case, is a couple that were victims of, what we call “Spiking”.
So they either put spikes on the road or just rocks, they want you to pull over.
And that is where you get robbed… or even worse…
Derek Link
I'm walking along the very busy N4 highway in the North West. Why am I telling you this? Because this highway can be a death trap and not just because of negligent drivers…
VO:
The Bakwena N1,N4 route is the gateway to various industries, including mines and tourism. With about 13000 vehicles passing through the Marikana Toll Plaza daily, it’s no surprise that accidents are a regular occurrence.
Jerry Bouwer:
The scenes are never the same. It’s traumatic. Women and children,it will always stay with you, and it is always uncomfortable driving past these previous scenes and incidents where the lives were taken of innocent people.
You have to deal with your own personal life, and then you have to deal with patients and those around them as well.
VO:
Jerry Bouwer is a Paramedic and owner of Hartbeespoort Emergency Medical Services. H.E.M.S. operates in and around the Brits area. He knows about the dangers of the N4 all too well.
Jerry:
We’ve seen how bad these incidents are and it is not safe for anyone.
VO:
Not all incidents on the N4 are because of criminal activities, however Jerry has noticed an upward trend in spiking incidents. These attacks occur mostly at night and are often violent. Jerry recalls one particularly disturbing incident in 2019.
Jerry:
We received a call early on a Friday morning, just after 4 O'Clock. The dispatch just said that there was a piece of concrete that was thrown off a bridge, through the windscreen. I remember arriving on scene and it was literally a bloodbath.
The only thing I remember was that we left the house,
I showed her something.
That was it, I woke up in hospital.
VO: The Roos’ family, JC, Claudia and thei r 13 month old daughter were travelling in the vehicle when the concrete smashed through the windscreen and hit J.C. in the face. He lost consciousness, but Claudia remembers everything.
Claudia:
When we finally came to a stop,
I checked to see if my child was hurt.
She was fine, but in shock,
she did not know what was going on.
My husband was in a lot of pain.
When I saw him, I immediately knew he was in a lot of pain.
His jaw was hanging here…
I thought he was dead.
LINK:
Their vehicle ended up here, it didn't roll, how I don't know, but there’s Claudia sitting in the vehicle next to J.C., he is covered in blood, it's dark, cars are going by, she doesn't know what to do, she's panicking. Then a knock on the door, help it last, no. A gun in her face!
Claudia:
I saw the gun pointing at me, but I looked away.
He then wanted to get into the vehicle.
First ON my daughter’s side, THEN HE came around to the driver’s WINDOW.
He then demanded money,
I told him, I don’t have any money.
I showed the phones to him, he had a look,
he looked at J.C. and he then ran away.
VO: After the criminal left, Claudia could once again focus on her husband. It was clear that his life was hanging in the balance. Help finally arrived and JC had to be flown to Milpark Hospital in Johannesburg.
Claudia:
I had to say goodbye to him.
That was a terrible feeling.
But we are here today.
And it is amazing.
JC:
Some doctors cannot believe that I survived.
I shouldn’t be alive after all of that.
I had two big operations,
to remove teeth that were in my airways,
and another to reconstruct my face.
We made it through.
I am back at work. Slowly but surely, I’ve improved.
VO: The Roos’s accident happened three years ago, and yet it seems very little has changed. During our filming, another vehicle was attacked after hitting rocks close to the Brits Plaza. Shots were fired at the vehicle, and the passenger ran away. The Police Service was searching for the passenger the next morning and our cameras were there to capture it. The person was still missing at the time of filming.
LINK:
Bakwena warn Motorists about travelling on the N1 / N4 highway at night and we did see the patrol vehicles while we were out filming, but are they doing enough?
Jerry:
They are generating an income from the N4, so part of that should be making sure that the guys travelling on that route are safe. There are low lighting areas and that is where these incidents are occuring.
Derek:
Motorists should be warned.
Jerry:
Motorists should definitely be warned. And I think it has come to the point where it is not safe for anyone to travel alone anymore.
Break before hectic Interview
Jerry Upsound:
We are on our way for a MVA, on the N4, a motor Vehicle accident, but there are 4 critical patients, 4 priority 1 patients on scene.

When I receive a call like this, on my way to the response car, it’s a quick prayer, just to keep everybody on that scene, those families, myself and my team, to keep us safe.
VO:
When his team receives a call that a vehicle is next to the road and medical assistance is required, they prepare for the worst. That’s what happened after a call in early May…
Jerry:
They said there were rocks involved, shots were fired, and there was already somebody laying down. We knew it was going to be bad. And on arrival on that scene, it has just proven to be exactly what it sounded like.
Johanette:
The tyre hit something. At that moment we thought it was rocks. And we continued to drive for a bit. He said he does not know what the damage was to the vehicle, but we can’t stop now. Why he stopped I can’t confirm for you… but he did.
VO:
Johanette, and their baby girl Annabelle, were waiting inside the vehicle as Juandré tried to fix the tyre.
Johanette:
He just screamed: “No! No!, please take everything. You can have everything. Just give me my wife and my child”
And immediately I knew.
The one man tried to drag me out of the vehicle and I was busy grabbing Annabelle and that's when Jeandré stepped forward, the man shot him and Jeandré fell and he shot him again and he turned to me and started shooting at me and Annabelle.
So I remember two shots firing, one shot missed me and one shot hit me in the shoulder. I grabbed Annabelle and the man tried pulling me out and try to grab Annabelle from me.
And so I just grabbed Annabelle, and I put her against her father and I went to lie on top of her.
Just begging them not to hurt me because I was so scared for her life, I mean…
Derek:
But they tried to take Annabelle?
Johanette:
They did, the guy literally, put his hands around her trying to take her and at that moment, I'm sorry for saying this, but you don't care how badly you hurt your child, just to keep her, and so that's when I put her underneath me on the ground.
Derek:
Next to Juandré?
Johanette: Yes, well it was the only shelter I could find.
Derek:
Was Juandré still breathing?
No, no, I don’t think he was.

I can't explain to you the difference of feeling between someone who's sleeping, the weight and the feel of their arm, and someone who’s just… there's no life anymore so I knew…
I knew, I knew instantly but I got up and I ran, with Annabelle, to find help for Juandré. Because you know, you're hopeful….
VO: Juandré’s father, Brian Kidson rushed to the crime scene that evening, insisting on seeing his son’s body.
Derek: Juandré was lying here?
Bryan: Juandré was lying here, the car was standing there, he was lying here. With his feet to the road and his face in the grass, the grass was still long.
It is so cruel, I don’t know what went through those people’s minds to kill my son like that…

Derek:
The police, have they told you musch about the follow-up?

The last time I phoned they said they are still scratching. That’s the only news we got.
I think it is very important to try and catching these people, start to bring them to justice for what they have done. They still need to go through the system.
Johanette:
Knowing that your husband just died, you saw it, your child saw it. Even though she is just one year old. It’s something you can't explain to anyone.

He was a very amazing person.
Derek:
And he loved his baby daughter?
Yes… so much.

That's the whole point of us speaking to the media is just trying to create awareness that don't stop,

Drive to somewhere safe, a garage.

Just don’t stop next to the N4.
